summary: A GPU worker that fails mid-step stops the engine at once, and the server exits with status 1 so a restart policy can bring it back
compatibility: No user action required. To have the server restart after such a failure, run the container with a restart policy (for example --restart on-failure).
details: When one tensor-parallel rank failed inside a step, for example with a CUDA out-of-memory error on TP1, its peers could stay blocked in a collective the failed rank never joined. The engine read replies in rank order and only from the output rank, so the server stayed up but answered nothing until VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (300 s) ran out.

Every rank now reports its failure, including ranks that do not return the step's output, and the engine reads replies from all ranks in any order (includes #917). The first failure stops the engine within a second, and the log names the failing rank and its error.
When the server stops because its engine failed, it now exits with status 1 instead of 0, so Docker's on-failure policy and other supervisors see a crash.
Waiting for a step still spins while replies are frequent, so decode speed is unchanged (GLM-5.3-Flash Spark TP2: steps/s within 0.4%).
